text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
THE NEWS
- The Mohajir National Movement (MQM) called for redeployment of army in Karachi to control the deteriorating law and order situation.
- The Interior Ministry has directed the provincial authorities and federal capital administration to set up rapid deployment forces to combat organised crime.
THE MUSLIM
- The government on Wednesday terminated 492 management trainee officers from the Oil and Gas Development Corporation.
THE NATION
- The Privatisation Commission has prepared two references on alleged irregularities in two deals carried out during the previous Benazir Bhutto-led PPP government.
DAWN
- Nine people were killed in different parts of Karachi on the second consecutive day of an undeclared strike over the killing of five MQM workers.

- Over 1,007 million rupees in loans were written off by three nationalised banks in the last three to four years, according to provisional figures submitted by the State (central) Bank of Pakistan in the Lahore High Court.

- Envoys of the Aid-to-Pakistan Consortium countries have endorsed the broad economic measures contained in the 1997/98 (July-June) budget proposals and said the steps would help improve the overall economic situation in the country.
- Mir Aimal Kansi, suspected of attacking CIA headquarters in Langley, Virginia, was arrested by the U.S. law enforcement authorities in Pakistan and sent to the United States.

- Balochistan province Chief Minister Akhtar Mengal, who also holds the finance portfolio, presented the 1997/98 budget in the provincial assembly, with an outlay of over 19.81 billion rupees without levying new taxes.
- The government has finalised a proposal to wind up several sections at 18 embassies abroad to cut non-development spending.

- Foreign secretaries of Pakistan and India are due to formally resume on Friday the second round of talks to evolve a mechanism and agenda for discussing bilateral issues, including the Jammu and Kashmir dispute.
- Heads of four major banks said they might cut lending rates shortly, but did not say when or by how much.
- Business on most commodity markets in Karachi remained at a standstill for a second day as buyers and sellers stayed away because of tension after the killing of MQM activists.
- All the major state-owned units in power, oil and gas, financial and industrial and communications sectors will be privatised in 1997/98.
